correctness.rationale: Phase-preserving position resets with symmetric switch rate nu produce coupled backward equations D m0 double prime+nu(m1-m0)=-1 and D m1 double prime+nu(m0-m1)+rho(m1(0)-m1)=-1. B=[[nu,-nu],[-nu,nu+rho]], E=exp[-a sqrt(B/D)], H=(I-E)B^-1, e=E 1,h=H 1 give m1(0)=h1/e1 and m0(0)=h0+(1-e0)h1/e1. Eigenvalues b_±=nu+rho/2 ±sqrt(nu²+rho²/4) prove M~a/(2 sqrt(D nu)) as nu↓0 and M=T(rho/2)-(rho²/(8 nu))T prime(rho/2)+O(nu^-2) as nu→∞ with T(s)=(exp(a sqrt(s/D))-1)/s. T prime changes sign at z*=1.593624..., so z>z* yields some finite nu below infinite-speed limit and a global finite minimizer by continuity/coercivity. No uniqueness or converse claimed. Independent 2x2 eigenchecks verify fast correction and slow sqrt singularity; slow check requires sufficiently tiny nu due to large regular part.
